summary: 企业把人才视作固定而易辨认的特质，可能错估员工，也可能错失培养机会。文章逐一检验明星员工能否识别、业绩能否准确归因，以及组织信念如何影响人的成长。
logic: 分析识人与评估的误差
考察组织信念和培养投入

paragraphs.brief: 对人才的一个普遍看法是，人才是一种合理的固定特征，因此，物色、招聘和留住明星演员是各组织的工作。
sentences: One widely held assumption about talent is that it is a reasonably fixed characteristic and it is therefore the job of organisations to identify, recruit and retain star performers.
对人才的一个普遍看法是，人才是一种合理的固定特征，因此，物色、招聘和留住明星演员是各组织的工作。
This belief affects the way people are managed in the workplace.
这种信念影响到工作场所的管理方式。
Most recruitment decisions are influenced by the skills and abilities of an individual rather than their aptitude and attitude.
大多数征聘决定都受到个人技能和能力的影响，而不是受到其才能和态度的影响。
In terms of career development, organisations invest in staff who have been selected to reach higher-level positions, while ignoring front-line employees and people with less perceived potential.
在职业发展方面，各组织对被选任担任较高职位的工作人员进行投资，而忽视第一线雇员和潜力较低的人。
This idea, that talent is a fixed, identifiable characteristic – and that those firms with the best people do the best – is both flawed and harmful to people and organisations.
这种想法，即人才是一种固定的、可识别的特点 — — 那些拥有最优秀人才的公司做得最好 — — 既存在缺陷，又对人和组织有害。
There is a lot of evidence on this point, and it is useful to highlight some of the most pertinent arguments.
关于这一点有许多证据，强调一些最相关的论点是有益的。

paragraphs.brief: 更有趣的问题不是恒星的存在，而是这些恒星是否可以可靠地识别，更重要的是，这些恒星的才华是固定的方面，还是可以改变的方面。
sentences: First, are there stars?
首先，有星星吗？
There is no question that in every field, from sports to computer programming to music, there are people who are better than the rest.
毫无疑问，从体育到计算机编程到音乐，每个领域都有比其他人更好的人。
As psychologist Dean Keith Simonton, who has spent his career studying greatness, has said, ‘Wherever you look, the same story can be told.
作为心理学家迪恩·基思·西蒙顿(Dean Keith Simonton)，他毕生都在学习伟大，他说，“无论你看到什么，都可以讲同样的故事。
Identify the ten per cent who have achieved the most in a certain endeavour.
确定在某一项努力中取得最大成就的10%。
Count the accomplishments they have to their credit.
数数他们的成就他们的功劳。
Now tally the accomplishments of the remaining 90 per cent.
现在清点其余90%的成就。
The first tally will equal or surpass the second.’
第一个计数将等于或超过第二个。

For instance, in music, 16 individuals have produced about 50 per cent of the Western classical music that is performed and recorded today, while another 235 composers have produced the remaining half.
例如，在音乐方面，有16人制作了约50%的西方古典音乐，今天播放和录制，另有235名作曲家制作了其余一半。

The more interesting questions concern not the existence of stars, but whether these stars can be reliably identified and, even more importantly, whether their talent is a fixed aspect or can be altered.
更有趣的问题不是恒星的存在，而是这些恒星是否可以可靠地识别，更重要的是，这些恒星的才华是固定的方面，还是可以改变的方面。

paragraphs.brief: 此外，对业绩和能力的判决取决于用来判断什么是好，什么是坏的标准。
sentences: Identifying the best people is tricky.
找到最好的人很难
Quality of performance changes over time and this is true whether we are talking about professors or footballers.
演艺质量随时间而变化，无论我们谈论的是教授还是足球运动员，都是如此。
If performance naturally varies, any measurement taken at a single point in time, such as when someone is being hired, will have error and imprecision.
如果性能自然不同，在某一时间点，如有人被雇用时，任何计量都会有错误和不精确。
Therefore, single assessments of talent are likely to contain mistakes in their categorisation of people.
因此，对人才的单一评估可能包含对人的分类方面的错误。
Also, judgements about performance and ability depend on the standards used to judge what is good and bad.
此外，对业绩和能力的判决取决于用来判断什么是好，什么是坏的标准。
It should surprise no-one that for Bach to be considered a great musician, standards of music needed to change to embrace the qualities that his compositions possessed.
巴赫要被视为伟大的音乐家音乐的标准必须改变才能接受他作品的品质
Similarly, artists and art come in and out of fashion, which means that what is genius depends not only on a person’s ability, but on the prevailing standards used to evaluate output.
艺术家和艺术也出自时尚，这意味着天才不仅取决于个人的能力，也取决于评估产出的通行标准。

paragraphs.brief: 最后，很难准确评估人及其能力。
sentences: Finally, it is difficult to evaluate people and their abilities with precision.
最后，很难准确评估人及其能力。
In the domain of work, research shows that the best predictors of job performance tend to be measures of intelligence.
在工作领域，研究表明，对工作业绩的最佳预测往往是对情报的衡量。
But even these measures correlate only loosely with performance, which means that more than 80 per cent of the variation in performance is unexplained by even the best predictors.
但是，即使这些措施也与业绩关系不大，这意味着80%以上的业绩差异甚至由最佳预测者来解释。
Even in the sports arena, where one would think natural ability would be readily assessed because sports teams spend lots of resources on identifying talent, mistakes get made.
即使在体育领域，人们也会认为自然能力会很容易地得到评估，因为体育队花费了大量资源来识别人才，就会犯错误。

Basketball star Michael Jordan was dropped by his high-school basketball coach and a number of top American football quarterbacks were available early in their careers because they were not considered good enough by various teams.
篮球明星迈克尔·乔丹被他的高中篮球教练丢弃不少美国足球四分卫在职业生涯的早期就已经出任因为他们被各队认为不够好

paragraphs.brief: 因此，业绩可能既是培训的结果，也是培训的内在能力，这表明，如何管理人们可以改变业绩。
sentences: This leads on to the next question: is talent born or made?
这引出下一个问题：人才是天生的还是创造的？

Should organisations assume that almost anyone can become a star performer, which implies that there ought to be a greater emphasis on motivation and development, or do they just figure out who is good and who isn’t?
组织应该假设，几乎任何人都可以成为明星表演者，这意味着应该更加强调动机和发展，还是它们只是发现谁是好人和谁是坏人？

Here the evidence is clear: talent is at least as much ‘created’ as inherent and, more importantly, the customary way companies think about identifying talent almost certainly works to destroy a lot of untapped potential.
这里的证据是明确的：人才的创造至少与内在的一样多，更重要的是，公司对确定人才的习惯思维几乎肯定会摧毁许多尚未开发的潜力。

Decades of research by K. Anders Ericsson, professor of psychology at Florida State University, show that exceptional performance doesn’t happen without around ten years of nearly daily, deliberate practice for about four hours a day, by people who, with the assistance of their coaches, have access to the best techniques.
佛罗里达州立大学心理学教授K. Anders Ericsson的数十年研究显示，如果没有大约10年的每日、每天约4小时的蓄意练习，那些在教练的协助下有机会获得最佳技术的人就不会有出色的表演。
Once achieved, exceptional performance can’t be maintained without relentless effort.
一旦取得成绩，如果没有不懈的努力，就无法保持非凡的业绩。
So performance may be as much a consequence of training as it is of innate ability, which suggests that performance can be altered by how people are managed.
因此，业绩可能既是培训的结果，也是培训的内在能力，这表明，如何管理人们可以改变业绩。

paragraphs.brief: 将人才视为固定的和工作表现，作为将人分类的一种方式，可以产生一种自我实现的预言，在这种预言中，能力和智慧确实会变得固定。
sentences: Further research by Stanford psychology professor Carol Dweck shows that the tendency of organisations to see performance results as an opportunity for an ‘assessment’ of ability, results in lower performance and poor motivation.
斯坦福心理学教授Carol Dweck的进一步研究表明，各组织倾向于将业绩结果视为对能力进行 " 评估 " 的机会，这导致业绩下降和动机不良。

Dweck identified two sets of goals that people bring to a performance context: ‘performance goals, where the purpose is to validate one’s ability or avoid demonstrating a lack of ability, and learning goals, where the aim is to acquire new knowledge and skills’.
Dweck确定了人们在业绩方面带来的两套目标：" 业绩目标，目的是验证一个人的能力或避免显示缺乏能力；学习目标，目的是获得新的知识和技能 "。
People with performance goals have been shown to be more prone to helpless behaviour and debilitation after a setback, while people with learning goals strive for higher performance.
业绩目标显示，有学习目标的人在遭遇挫折后更容易出现无助行为和虚弱状态，而有学习目标者则努力追求更高的业绩。
The implications for managing people and talent are clear.
管理人员和人才所涉及的问题显而易见。
Seeing talent as fixed and job performance as a way of classifying people creates a self-fulfilling prophecy in which ability and intelligence do become fixed.
将人才视为固定的和工作表现，作为将人分类的一种方式，可以产生一种自我实现的预言，在这种预言中，能力和智慧确实会变得固定。
By contrast, seeing ability as malleable leads to a different sort of self-fulfilling prophecy, in which individuals and their employers may invest in ways to enhance performance.
相比之下，将能力视为可塑性导致一种不同的自我实现预言，个人及其雇主可以在这种预言中投资于提高业绩的方式。

items.en: disagreement with the view that employing talented people enables companies to achieve top performance
items.zh: 认为雇用有才华的人可使公司取得最佳业绩的观点
items.why: A 段先提出“拥有最好人才的公司表现最好”这一假设，接着明确批评它有缺陷、还会对个人与组织造成伤害。

items.en: a description of what individuals have to do on a regular basis to improve their performance
items.zh: 说明个人为改进业绩必须经常开展的工作
items.why: E 段用埃里克松对杰出表现者的研究解释，卓越技能需要长期、规律而有针对性的练习。

items.en: the evidence that exceptional talent exists in all areas of life
items.zh: 在所有生活领域都存在杰出人才的证据
items.why: B 段并列体育、编程和音乐，指出每个领域都确实有超出其他人的表现者，回答卓越人才是否广泛存在。

items.en: how different ways of evaluating achievement at work can cause different reactions in employees
items.zh: 工作成绩评价的不同方式如何引起雇员的不同反应
items.why: F 段分析两种评价取向：把成绩当作固定能力的测验会损害动力，把能力看作可发展则会鼓励学习和投入。

items.en: the belief that the time when an assessment is carried out affects its accuracy
items.zh: 认为进行评估的时间影响评估的准确性
items.why: C 段指出人的表现会自然波动，所以在招聘等单一时间点作评估会有误差，直接说明评估时机影响准确性。

items.en: the extent to which different talented individuals have contributed to their particular area of achievement
items.zh: 不同才智人士对其特定成就领域所作贡献的程度
items.why: B 段用少数作曲家占据大量演出和录音曲目的比例，量化不同个人对同一领域贡献的集中程度。

items.en: How many Western classical composers are identified as exceptionally talented?
items.zh: 有多少西方古典作曲家被确定为超有才华？
items.why: 问“有多少位被认定为特别有才华的西方古典作曲家? ”此处的16 人就是那批“star” 作曲家。填数字 16.

items.en: Which composer initially received little recognition for his work?
items.zh: 哪个作曲家最初的工作没有得到什么认可？
items.why: 说明巴赫需要后来评价标准改变才被认为伟大 = 早期认可度低。

items.en: Who can help improve the performance of people practising daily?
items.zh: 谁能帮助提高日常执业者的业绩？
items.why: 问“谁能帮助每天练习的人提高表现? "一 coaches (教练)。

groups.label: 简答题
groups.instructionsZh: 根据原文简答。每题最多填两个词，可含数字。

items.en: Companies usually hire people on the basis of their character.
items.zh: 公司通常根据其性质雇用人员。
items.why: 题干说“公司通常依据品格招聘"。原文说主要依据技能与能力，而非态度/资质 = 相矛盾。

items.en: There are some areas of sport that have a greater proportion of talent than others.
items.zh: 有些体育领域的人才比例高于其他领域。
items.why: 原文说从体育到音乐、编程，各领域都有表现出众的人。它没有统计不同体育项目中人才的比例，无法作项目间比较。

items.en: Measures of intelligence accurately predict performance at work.
items.zh: 情报量度准确预测了工作业绩。
items.why: 题干称智力测量准确预测工作表现。原文说相关性很弱 = 错误。

items.en: There are cases in which talented sportspeople have been overlooked.
items.zh: 在有些情况下，有才华的运动员被忽视。
items.why: 乔丹曾被高中篮球教练淘汰，多位顶尖四分卫早期也被球队低估。这些例子直接证明运动天才可能得不到及时识别。

items.en: Newly formed organisations have the most highly motivated staff.
items.zh: 新组建的组织的工作人员积极性最高。
items.why: 研究将员工动力与组织如何评价能力联系起来，没有按组织成立时间比较员工动力，也没有说新组织的员工动力最高。

pairs: 前者是正式的名词短语，后者是日常动词表达，都指公司表现最出色。段落质疑的是人才必然带来这种结果的看法。
题干问谁能帮练习者提高表现，原文改用名词 assistance，引出提供帮助的教练。
原文用运动、编程和音乐为例，说明各个领域都有人表现出众。
points: B 段并列体育、编程和音乐，指出每个领域都确实有超出其他人的表现者，回答卓越人才是否广泛存在。
题干说“公司通常依据品格招聘"。原文说主要依据技能与能力，而非态度/资质 = 相矛盾。
clauses: As psychologist Dean Keith Simonton, …, has said, ‘Wherever you look, the same story can be told.
“who has spent his career studying greatness”修饰前面的 Simonton。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 who 时，回看 Simonton，再把修饰信息接回主句。
For instance, in music, 16 individuals have produced about 50 per cent of the Western classical music that is performed and recorded today, ….
连接词 while 引出“while another 235 composers have produced the remaining half”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: Most organisations are looking for talent.
大多数组织都在寻找人才。
But what if they’ve got it wrong, asks Jeffrey Pfeffer
但如果他们弄错了，问杰弗里·费弗
